body:
New on the site: River Fox Train in West Sacramento. Their railbikes run on century-old tracks along the Sacramento River — a 10-mile round trip through Yolo farmland, with an electric-assist motor for when little legs (or big ones) get tired.

The details that matter: seated riders need to be 3 or older (under 3 rides in a front-facing carrier), and each bike holds two riders up to 600 lbs combined. Weekday railbikes are $68.90 per rider, booked through their site. The same depot also runs themed train rides — beer, boba, murder mystery — for the grown-up outings.

Free library storytimes, right on your city page
excerpt: Sacramento Public Library storytimes for babies through preschoolers now show up in the This week section of every SacMoms city page.
body:
If you have a baby, toddler or preschooler, library storytime is the easiest outing in town. Sacramento Public Library runs them at branches across the county, built for kids 0 to 5 and their grown-ups, with older siblings welcome. The library describes them as songs, rhymes, movement and stories, and some branches add play time afterward so you can meet other families.

The hard part has always been finding which branch has one on the morning you are free. So SacMoms pulls the library's own listing and folds the next seven days of storytimes into the This week section of each city page, sorted by distance from you. Every listing links back to the library's page, so you can check the exact time and room before you head out.

Find this week's storytimes near you: Elk Grove, Sacramento, Rancho Cordova, Folsom or Citrus Heights.

title: Apple Hill: the classic fall day trip from Sacramento
excerpt: Over 50 family farms near Placerville with you-pick orchards, pumpkin patches and bake shops. How to plan a day there with kids.
body:
Every fall, half of Sacramento seems to drive up Highway 50 to Apple Hill, and with kids it is easy to see why. The Apple Hill Growers association covers more than 50 family farms in the foothills near Placerville, between Sacramento and Lake Tahoe: you-pick orchards, pumpkin patches, bake shops and farms with activities just for kids.

A few things make the day easier. Pick two or three farms before you go instead of trying to see them all; the growers' site has a printable map and a list of which farms are open right now. Their harvest calendar shows what is ripe when, so you know whether you are walking into apples or just pies. The roads up there are narrow and winding, so leave room in the plan for slow traffic and a carsick kid or two.

Apple Hill is not only a fall thing, either. The growers also list Christmas tree farms, so it is worth a second trip in December.

title: Rainy-day plan: four big indoor spots around Sacramento
excerpt: The first rain is here. Four museums worth a whole morning with kids, plus where to find indoor open play near you.
body:
Once the rain starts, the parks empty out and everyone needs a plan B. These four are big enough to fill a morning and all within easy reach of the city.

Sacramento Children's Museum, Rancho Cordova. Hands-on, play-based exhibits for toddlers through early elementary. Tiny Tuesday is a time set aside for children 24 months and under. sackids.org

SMUD Museum of Science and Curiosity (MOSAC), Sacramento. More than 100 hands-on science exhibits on Jibboom Street, plus a planetarium with shows for kids. Reserve planetarium tickets ahead. visitmosac.org

California State Railroad Museum, Old Sacramento. Real restored locomotives to walk through, an activity center for kids, and a storytime of its own. Train-loving kids will not want to leave. californiarailroad.museum

Aerospace Museum of California, McClellan. Hands-on STEM exhibits and the Flight Zone, where instructors run flight simulators for kids and adults. Call ahead to reserve a simulator slot. aerospaceca.org

Want something shorter, like an hour of climbing and bouncing? Every city page has an Indoor filter for open play gyms and play cafes near you, and the Places page lists them all.

title: A fall walk at Effie Yeaw Nature Center
excerpt: 100 acres of river woodland in Carmichael with easy trails, wild deer and turkeys, and a nature center full of rescued native animals.
body:
If your kids have never seen a deer up close, Effie Yeaw Nature Center is the place. It sits on the American River Parkway in Carmichael, with 100 acres of riverside woodland and easy, signed trails that small legs can manage. Families regularly spot deer, wild turkeys, squirrels, hawks and owls, and fall is a lovely time to go, with the oaks turning and the light low.

Inside, the nature center cares for nearly 30 native animals that cannot be released back into the wild, and a small exhibit hall covers the natural and cultural history of the river. Picnics are allowed, so pack lunch. One rule to know before you go: to protect the wildlife, dogs, bikes and horses are not allowed in the preserve, not even a dog in your arms.

The center also runs family programs and kids' classes through the season. The ones near you show up in the This week section of the Sacramento page.

Effie Yeaw Nature Center →

title: Salmon season at Nimbus Fish Hatchery
excerpt: Chinook salmon are coming home up the American River. A free outing in Gold River where kids can see where they end up.
body:
Every fall, Chinook salmon swim back up the American River to the place they were raised, and the Nimbus Fish Hatchery in Gold River is where you can see the end of that trip. The state hatchery raises salmon and steelhead for release into the river, and its busy season for salmon runs from the beginning of November through mid-December. Steelhead follow in January and February.

It is free to visit. There is a visitor center, a fish ladder (closed March through October), and a short nature trail along the river right next to the American River Parkway. The hatchery also runs monthly public tours with no sign-up and a Tot Time for kids 2 to 7 with a grown-up; check their page for the next dates.

Before you go, look at the hatchery's page for closures, since hours can change with staffing and weather. For more to do on that side of the county, see the Rancho Cordova page.

Nimbus Fish Hatchery →

title: Sandhill cranes are back at Cosumnes River Preserve
excerpt: About 3,000 sandhill cranes spend the winter south of Elk Grove. When to go, where to walk, and what to bring.
body:
One of the best free shows in the county is happening just south of Elk Grove. Roughly 3,000 lesser and greater sandhill cranes spend the winter at the Cosumnes River Preserve, and prime viewing runs from mid-October to the start of March. They are tall, loud and easy for kids to spot, especially when big groups fly in together.

Dawn and dusk are when you see the most cranes. Keep your distance and your voices low, since feeding cranes spook easily. The Lost Slough Wetlands Boardwalk is a one-mile, wheelchair-accessible loop with ramps and rails, a good fit for little walkers. It keeps daytime hours, so check the preserve's page before planning a dusk visit. The visitor center on Franklin Boulevard is staffed by volunteers on weekends.

Pack snacks and water, since there is no food on site, and leave the dog at home: only service dogs are allowed. For more nearby, see the Elk Grove page.

title: Holiday picks for Thanksgiving weekend and December
excerpt: A holiday market at Effie Yeaw, Winter Wonderland at Fairytale Town, a kids' night out, and which spots close on Thanksgiving Day.
body:
The holiday calendar fills up fast. Here are the family events around Sacramento we would put on the fridge now.

Effie Yeaw Holiday Market, Saturday Nov 28. The nature center's annual market of handmade, local gifts, with warm drinks, in Carmichael. An easy Thanksgiving-weekend outing with a walk on the trails after. Event page

Winter Wonderland at Fairytale Town, Dec 5 to 6 and 12 to 13. Santa visits, a Grinch appearance, crafts, a scavenger hunt, holiday lights at dusk and a snowfall each evening. It is ticketed, under 2s are free, and grown-ups need to bring a kid to get in. Event page

Kids' Night Out: Cocoa and Cookies, Friday Dec 11. A drop-off evening at Fairytale Town with crafts, games and dinner for kids 4 and up, so the grown-ups get a night off. Registration is required and space is limited. Event page

Noon Year's Eve at the Sacramento Zoo, Dec 31. On the zoo's events list now; check back there for details. Zoo events

One heads-up for Thanksgiving Day itself, Nov 26: the Sacramento Children's Museum, MOSAC and Fairytale Town are all closed. More seasonal events show up in the Special events section of the Sacramento page as they are announced.

title: Thanksgiving weekend with kids: what's on, Thursday to Sunday
excerpt: A family turkey trot, the one rink open on Thanksgiving Day, what reopens Friday, Theatre of Lights and the Dickens Street Faire.
body:
Thanksgiving is tomorrow, and a four-day weekend with kids needs a plan beyond the table. Here is what is on around Sacramento from Thursday morning to Sunday, and what is closed.

Thanksgiving morning: a family turkey trot. Run to Feed the Hungry in East Sacramento is the big one, a loop from J Street by Sac State through tree-lined East Sac streets, with a 10K and a 5K that you can walk. The race FAQ says strollers are welcome if they start in the walking corral, and dogs stay home. Race day info In Folsom, the Folsom Turkey Trot is billed as a family fun run, starting from the Rodeo Park and Lions Park area on Stafford Street. There is no sign-up on race morning, so check its site today if you still need a spot. Folsom Turkey Trot

Open on Thanksgiving Day: the Downtown Sacramento Ice Rink. The rink at Ali Youssefi Square on K Street keeps shorter holiday hours on Thanksgiving, which makes it a good way to burn energy before dinner. The smallest rental skate is a youth size 8, and the rink suggests age 3 and up. It is outdoors and closes in heavy rain, so call ahead if the sky looks grey. Ice rink page

Closed on Thanksgiving Day. The Sacramento Zoo, Fairytale Town, the Sacramento Children's Museum and MOSAC are all closed on Thursday, Nov 26.

Friday: the museums are back. The Children's Museum reopens for play on Friday, and MOSAC is open all through Thanksgiving week apart from Thursday. Fairytale Town is open Friday to Sunday, weather permitting, and the zoo is back to its usual schedule. Children's Museum · MOSAC

Friday night: Theatre of Lights starts its weekend run. Old Sacramento's light-and-story show plays on the rooftops and balconies of K Street on Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights from Nov 27 until Christmas Eve, with no show on Thanksgiving. It is outdoors, and shows can change with the weather. Theatre of Lights

Saturday: Dickens Street Faire in Old Town Elk Grove. Expect free kids' activities at the Old Town Plaza, photos with Santa, a fire department Santa rescue, carols and a story with Mr. and Mrs. Claus, and the town tree lighting on Walnut Street that evening. Event page The same day, the Effie Yeaw Holiday Market in Carmichael is on too, from last week's holiday picks.

If it rains. MOSAC and the Children's Museum cover a wet Friday, and our rainy-day plan has all four big indoor spots. Your city page lists more indoor places near you, starting with Sacramento.

Happy Thanksgiving from SacMoms. We are thankful for every parent who passes this site along.
